children: , the semiconductor and infrastructure-software giant, slipped approximately 0.5% to $367.83 Wednesday ahead of its after-hours earnings report. The bar is towering. Investors want fresh evidence that explosive demand for Broadcom's custom AI accelerators can keep outrunning already sky-high expectations.

The numbers have been huge. Broadcom's second-quarter results delivered $22.19 billion in revenue, up 48%, with AI semiconductor sales reaching $10.8 billion. Management then set an even hotter third-quarter target: approximately $29.4 billion in total revenue and $16 billion from AI, implying growth of more than 200%.

AI would represent roughly 54.4% of Broadcom's third-quarter revenue guidance, up from 48.7% in the previous quarter. The picture shows another reason tonight matters: at $367.83, the stock sits 4.84% above its $350.86 GF Value estimate. A revenue beat may grab the headline, but margins, hyperscaler spending and free-cash-flow conversion will decide whether that premium survives.

title: Broadcom Slips 0.5% Before a $16 Billion AI Verdict
